Backup Depth & Deficiencies

The brief asks which 2nd, 3rd and 4th string players are being forced in. That question has two halves, and only one of them can be answered from official sources today. This page keeps them apart.

Half 1 — Observed absence OFFICIAL

Who is officially unavailable, and at which depth slot the club lists them. Read straight from the injury report and the club depth chart. No inference.

Half 2 — Replacement measured NOT AVAILABLE

Whether a backup actually took the snaps requires snap counts. No official snap-count source was verified, so this half is left blank rather than asserted. See F09.

Coverage: 31 of 32 clubs. nfl.com/depth-charts/ returns 404, so there is no league-wide official depth chart and each club’s own chart has to be captured one at a time. 31 clubs publish a chart as a readable table and are on this page. The one club that does not is Houston — its chart is published as an image, so it is left out rather than guessed (flag F16, source S46). Every club page calls its own chart unofficial.

Depth coverage by club

One row per club whose chart was captured. Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers do not play in Week 10, so they have no Week 10 injury report and their injury columns read 0. That is the league publishing nothing, not this page failing to find anything. Players charted counts names the club published. On own injury report counts how many of those names also appear on that same club’s Week 10 injury report, matched by exact name — no fuzzy matching, so a spelling difference shows up as a non-match rather than as a wrong merge. Blank slots are slots where the club published a string with no name in it.

Chart date is the date the club printed on its own chart. A blank means the club printed no date; it is not assumed to be the capture date.

First-string players carrying an official game status

These are the slots where a club’s own chart puts a player at first string and the league’s injury report gives that player an Out / Doubtful / Questionable status for Week 10. The next listed column is the next name the same club publishes at that same slot and string number.

Read the next-listed column for what it is. It is a statement about two published documents, not a prediction of who plays. A club’s chart is self-described as unofficial, a starter listed Questionable usually still plays, and snap counts are not available to confirm anything. Nothing here says a backup is the starter this week.

71 of 753 charted first-string slots carry an official Week 10 game status. Sorted by club.

Replacement depth — how deep past a ruled-Out first string

The table above records the fact of a replacement: the first string carries a status and the club publishes a next name. This table records the depth of that replacement. For every chart ladder whose first string carries an official game status (71 ladders — the same population as the table above), it reports how many strings the club's own chart must be read through before the first name the league has not ruled Out appears.

Definition, fixed before any value was computed. Replacement depth = the string number of the first charted name on the ladder whose game status is not Out, walking the club's own string order. Depth 1 means at least one name on the first string is not ruled Out — no replacement past the first string is required by the documents (the first string is Questionable or Doubtful, but not ruled Out). Depth 2 means every name on the first string is ruled Out and the second string holds a name that is not — and so on. Strings that are themselves ruled Out are skipped, so a depth is recorded only once a name that is not ruled Out is reached. Where the club publishes no name at an intermediate string, or every charted name on the ladder is ruled Out, the cell is blank and carries the reason in its hover text — never a guessed number.

Two depths are shown. The first counts only Out as a rule-out. The second, stricter one counts any listed game status (Out, Doubtful or Questionable) and therefore reports how deep the chart must be read before a name the league has said nothing about appears. A blank there means every charted name on that ladder carries a status.

What this does not say. It does not say who plays. No snap-count source was verified (F09), Houston has no machine-readable chart (F16), and a club's chart is self-described as unofficial. The numbers are arithmetic on two published documents — the club's depth chart and the league's injury report — and nothing more.

Replacement depth = string number of the first charted name on the ladder whose game status is not Out, in the club's own string order. A blank cell carries the reason in its hover text. Sorted by club, unit, ladder.

On a club’s injury report but not on that club’s own chart

51 players. This is a discrepancy between two official documents, so it is published rather than reconciled. The usual innocent reason is that an injured player was removed from the chart; the interesting reason is a name spelled differently in the two places. This page does not decide which, because deciding would be a guess. Where the two documents clearly disagree about who is on the team, that is recorded on Flagged for Review instead.

What this page will not do

  • It will not call a backup “the starter this week” without a snap-count source.
  • It will not rank depth beyond the club’s own published ordering, and that ordering is labelled unofficial.
  • It will not match two names by similarity. Equivalence is asserted only in data/depth-aliases.tsv, with the evidence recorded next to it.
  • It will not treat an absent player as injured. Absent and injured are different facts.
  • It will not fill Houston in from another source, because a depth chart is an ordering and no other official source publishes that ordering.

FL1 — NFL Line Lab — Verified data, open questions, and a strategy leaderboard that refuses to guess.

Data captured 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16 (UTC) from official league and club sources. Every value links to its source. Values that could not be confirmed from an official source are left blank and listed on Flagged for Review. Nothing on this site is a bet, an offer to wager, or advice. No price, edge or expected-value figure is displayed unless an official source supports it.
